_doc: The 1904 district's front yards (T-3203, T-3223): garden shrubs, young trees, a bed and ivy, each lot planted as its photograph shows it or, unpictured, in one of the period's few ways, and kept clear of every door, stoop, walk and fence. GENERATED by tools/plant_prairie_1904_front_yards.py from data/street_grid/1904.json, the 1904 sidecars' baked models and the traced Sanborn footprints -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. Local ENU metres of data/datum.json. shrubs and trees: [e, n, plant, height_m, crown_width_m, (grade if not the lot's), (stand_m, tub_m: a tub plant's, what its tub stands on over the ground and the tub's height)]; beds: [e, n, half_length_m, half_width_m, heading_deg, kind, scheme]; creeper: [e, n, facing_deg, width_m, height_m, ("mantle" on a stretch a picture shows wholly clothed, "mantle_sill" under a window in it: its top drawn level)]. The lawn is the ground's own sward.

arborvitae.name: American arborvitae, sheared to a cone

standard.name: evergreen clipped to a ball on a clear stem, in a tub

palm.name: palm from the palm house, set out in its tub

beds.round: a round bed cut in the lawn, bedded out

placement.note: Each plant's crown edge stands clear of the house's wall, every stoop and step, fence, coping and walk, a 2 m disk round every door, and a 5.2 m way from each front door to the lot line. Lots a photograph shows bare are bare. Seeded by the parcel's id.

tubs.note: Two clipped standards on clear stems, each in a square planting box with a dense leafy mass spilling over it, in the lawn before the conservatory's front, and tall shrubs along the far edge of the drive, as the 1894 Inland Architect plate and Lowe's c. 1897 photograph show them in summer. Inferred for 1 July 1904: the pictures are seven to ten summers before the scene, and boxed plants were wintered under glass.

bare.note: The photograph shows the yard bare before the porch.

creeper.note: Ivy over the west front and the porch, to about the second storey's sills and past them on the porch's piers (both Detroit Publishing views); a solid mantle over the whole ground storey of the front south of the portico and of the 18th Street flank west of the porte-cochere, up to the balcony's belt course (LC-D4-12551).

border.note: A dense border of shrubs inside the coping along 18th Street, east of the house (LC-D4-4a08066, right of the house), clear of the carriage ways.

stoop.note: Low shrubs at the foot of the porch, either side of its steps (LC-D4-4a08065).

trees.note: Young trees, staked, in the lawn between the coping and the house front (LC-D4-4a08065).

tubs.note: Clipped evergreens in tubs on and before the palm house's terrace and before the stable's arcade, as the 1894 Inland Architect plate shows them in summer (a ball on its tub, a ball on a clear stem, and a slim clipped column by the 18th Street wall's east pier, which Taylor's photograph 16555 shows too), with the cone by the wing's arched door and the palm set out before the drum that Taylor's photograph shows. Inferred for 1 July 1904: tub plants were wintered under glass and set out again each summer, and no picture nearer 1904 shows the terrace. Four slim clipped columns are planted in the terrace itself, not tubbed (a pair before the wing's arched windows and two at the drum's west side): Taylor's winter photograph 16554 shows all four and his summer 16555 three of them (the fourth behind the house's porch), so they stood the year round.

bare.note: The photograph shows the lawn open before the porch.
The photograph shows the lawn open to the house.
The photograph shows the lawn open either side of the stoop.
The photograph shows bare ground behind the iron fence.
The photograph shows the yard bare behind the iron fence.

creeper.note: Ivy over the north part of the front and the round bay to the third storey in the photograph; the print shows an electric lamp, so it is after 1904, and ivy of that reach was growing years before it.

bare.note: The photograph shows the yard bare behind the fence and posts.
